hero.headline: Palm Beach County man leads Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
hero.teaser: A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous road
hero.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled, weaving through traffic in an attempt to lose law enforcement before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

Deputies located Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Law enforcement deployed stop sticks to disable his vehicle near Interstate 95, bringing the dangerous pursuit to an end. However, Tillman refused to surrender peacefully after his vehicle was disabled.

After his car was stopped, Tillman bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot. Deputies caught up with him and took him into custody without further incident. The arrest ended a chase that put numerous motorists at risk as Tillman traveled at excessive speeds and forced vehicles off the road during his flight from law enforcement.

Tillman was arrested on multiple charges related to the chase and his driving behavior. He faces charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail. The incident highlights ongoing safety concerns on State Road 710, which has a reputation as one of the most dangerous roads in the area.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County return home after nearly 2 years of displacement
cards.body:
Residents of Villa Del Sol in St. Lucie County are returning to their condos after nearly two years of displacement due to structural damage. Residents were notified last month they could return to their units after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. The Board of Directors sent emails to residents informing them they could come back following a special inspection by engineers.

Katie Johnson was the first to share with WPTV that residents had been told they could return. She said she almost didn't believe it and that it was like too good to be true. Engineers sent a letter to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie described the work still underway at the property, noting that crews are still moving dirt back under the buildings. She reflected on the effort required to bring residents home, saying it's hard work.

Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot come back. He said their hearts were broken and they wanted to spend the rest of their lives there. Eric Johnson is among those not returning. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. He said it's been a terrible two years and the financial toll has been severe, noting they had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on.

Eric Johnson is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. He described the ongoing struggle, saying it's been a real struggle and that while he'd like to say they are finally starting to climb out of it, it still feels like they're kind of still falling and waiting to start climbing back up. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return, expressing that she just feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: Flip City gymnasts earn national top 15 finish, qualify for Junior Olympics in Iowa
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine have been competing as a unit throughout the season, each arriving at the sport through their own unique journey.

The trio found their way to gymnastics for different reasons. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really gymnastics at first, but rather the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by watching gymnasts on YouTube and seeing how amazing they were and how fun the sport looked. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things. Head Coach Candice Lazuka said the team had a strong season, competing locally and traveling before advancing to states and regionals.

At AAU Nationals last month, the gymnasts came remarkably close to a perfect score. Lazuka said the team scored a 9.9, noting that it is hard to get a perfect 10. The strong performance helped secure the team's top 15 finish and their qualification for the Junior Olympics, which will take place in Iowa next month.

The young gymnasts are excited about the upcoming competition. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings as happy and exciting at the same time. Rine has her sights set on a specific goal, saying she is focused on getting first place on floors at the Junior Olympics.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 with late goals to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two goals in the final five minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday in Atlanta.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. England took the lead when Anthony Gordon scored the opening goal in the 55th minute. Martinez said he dreamed it and told Alexis Mac Allister that he was going to score and win it. Messi had largely been kept quiet but fed the ball to Fernandez to sweep in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina attacks came wave after wave.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, the staff and the fans, saying the squad worked so hard to be there and falling short was just gutting. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team was ready to go home sad knowing they had left everything on the pitch, but after England scored they really proved themselves. England came up short in the World Cup semifinals for the third time after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018.

cards.headline: England and Argentina to renew fierce World Cup rivalry in Atlanta semifinal
cards.teaser: England and Argentina meet in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday in Atlanta, resuming one of the fiercest rivalries in international soccer.
cards.body:
England and Argentina resume one of the fiercest rivalries in international soccer when they meet in the World Cup semifinals in Atlanta on Wednesday. The winner will play Spain in the final in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday. The World Cup rivalry between the nations dates back to 1962, but it intensified with England's 1-0 win in the quarterfinals in 1966. Argentina captain Antonio Rattin, whose death was announced on Saturday, was sent off in a bad-tempered match. Twenty years later in Mexico, Diego Maradona scored the infamous Hand of God goal that helped Argentina to a 2-1 win in the quarterfinals. That game also saw Maradona score what many believe to be the greatest World Cup goal ever when he dribbled the ball from the halfway line before beating England goalkeeper Peter Shilton. In 1998, David Beckham was sent off for kicking out at Argentina midfielder Diego Simeone before England lost the round-of-16 game on penalties. Beckham scored a penalty in a 1-0 win four years later that contributed to Argentina being eliminated at the group stage.

Neither team has had a smooth ride to the semifinals. Argentina survived scares against Cape Verde and Egypt earlier in the knockout rounds and needed extra time to beat 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in the quarterfinals. England had to rally for wins against Congo and Norway after going a goal down and also beat co-host Mexico 3-2 in the round of 16 while down to 10 men. Lionel Messi has scored eight goals and provided crucial assists for Argentina. Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham both have six goals for England, with Bellingham scoring twice in each of England's last two games.

cards.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final with 2-0 win over France
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain beat France 2-0 Tuesday to reach its first World Cup final since 2010.
cards.body:
Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot after a play by teenager Lamine Yamal, and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday. A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne in the penalty area in the 22nd minute. After a poor first touch with his head, Digne was trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, who was playing in his 63rd game for France only six days before his 33rd birthday. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup marked the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in the tournament. It was his 30th goal in 60 international games for Spain.

Porro's give-and-go with Dani Olmo in the 58th minute put Spain up 2-0. Yamal was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after Porro's goal. Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Kylian Mbappé and France, FIFA's top-ranked team, were trying to become only the third team to reach three consecutive World Cup finals. They instead will play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday, the day before the final at MetLife Stadium across the river from New York City.

cards.headline: Florida Homeowner Faces Repairs After Hurricane Milton Destroys Roof Two Months After Paying Off Mortgage
cards.teaser: A Florida man paid off his house only to have Hurricane Milton tear off his roof two months later, leaving him to cover repair costs without home insurance.
cards.body:
A Florida homeowner who paid off his mortgage found himself facing major repair bills just two months later when Hurricane Milton tore the roof off his house. The man had no home insurance coverage at the time of the storm, forcing him to pay for the damage out of pocket.

Hurricane Milton caused extensive damage across Florida when it made landfall, with the storm's winds strong enough to rip roofing materials from structures. The homeowner's situation highlights the financial risks faced by Florida property owners who lack insurance coverage in a state regularly threatened by hurricanes.

The timing of the disaster compounded the financial burden for the homeowner, who had recently achieved the milestone of fully owning his property. He now must fund the entire cost of roof replacement and any related repairs without assistance from an insurance policy.

cards.headline: Atlanta increases security for England-Argentina World Cup semifinal
cards.teaser: Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta due to longstanding tensions between the two nations.
cards.body:
Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations stemming from the 1982 Falklands War. Videos circulating online appear to show England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami, where England played Norway over the weekend. Atlanta police said additional personnel and resources are already in place and will continue to be strategically assigned in and around event venues for Wednesday's match.

Argentina is the defending champion, while England has not won a World Cup since 1966. It is also the first time since England's World Cup win in 1966 that its national team has earned a berth in the semifinals. In addition to claiming three World Cup titles, Argentina has been the tournament's runner-up twice.

cards.headline: World Cup semifinals feature four highest-ranked teams
cards.teaser: The World Cup final four is set with France, Spain, England and Argentina advancing to the semifinals after weekend quarterfinal matches.
cards.body:
The World Cup's final four is now complete with France, Spain, England and Argentina advancing to the semifinals. Despite this being a tournament full of underdog success stories and surprise results, the last four consists of the four highest-ranked teams. England advanced after Jude Bellingham netted twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway in the quarterfinals. Argentina has Julián Alvarez to thank after the striker scored in extra time to help the team through to the semifinal against Switzerland. Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition for England.

Argentina is the defending champion and has scored the most goals out of anyone in the competition with 17. The team has relied on Lionel Messi to get it out of trouble, and the magic man has duly obliged so far. Many members of the current squad won the title back in 2022. France is considered by many to be the tournament favorite, with Kylian Mbappé proving superb with his pace and directness. Spain has conceded just one goal the entire tournament and beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024. Spain also beat France in the Nations League last year. The final is scheduled for July 19.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: Vero Beach parents sue city over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed and reburied without consent
hero.teaser: Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo allege their infant son's remains were disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and reinterred without their knowledge.
hero.body:
Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo have filed an amended lawsuit against the City of Vero Beach alleging their infant son's remains were disturbed during maintenance work at Crestlawn Cemetery and reburied without their knowledge or consent. The couple's son, identified in court documents only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old and was buried at the city-owned cemetery. The parents say they did not learn about what allegedly happened until April 2025, nearly 18 years after their son's burial.

According to the complaint, sometime between the 2007 burial and April 2025, heavy equipment being used for maintenance or irrigation work near the burial site breached the grave, damaging or destroying the casket, its contents, and the child's remains. The lawsuit alleges that someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket, and reinter the child without notifying the parents or obtaining their consent. The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment.

This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false but rather a ruling that the legal claims as originally pleaded could not proceed against the city under Florida law. The parents have now refiled with different legal arguments in an attempt to overcome the previous dismissal. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint. The City of Vero Beach has declined to comment on the amended complaint.

In court filings responding to the original lawsuit, the city disputed the allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage described by the parents. The city submitted a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C. The case highlights the legal protections cities have under Florida law and the challenges families face when seeking accountability for alleged mishandling of cemetery operations. The amended complaint represents the parents' continued effort to hold the city responsible for what they describe as the unauthorized disturbance and reburial of their infant son's remains.
